packets.title: S009 Al-Tawba CP01 vv001-016
paragraphs: Flag: NO BASMALA. Only surah in the 114 without it. Level 1: the written opening is Bara'a.

A dissociation from God and His Messenger to those with whom you made a compact among the associators. So travel in the land four months, and know that you will not frustrate God, and that God disgraces the unbelievers.

An announcement from God and His Messenger to the people on the day of the greater hajj: that God is dissociated from the associators, and His Messenger. If you repent it is better for you. If you turn away, know that you will not frustrate God. Give those who disbelieve news of a painful punishment — except those among the associators with whom you made a compact, then they did not fail you in anything and did not back anyone against you. Fulfill their compact to its term. God loves the God-fearing.

When the sacred months have slipped away, kill the associators wherever you find them. Take them, besiege them, sit for them at every ambush. If they repent and establish the prayer and give the zakāt, let them go their way. God is Forgiving, Merciful. If one of the associators seeks your protection, protect him until he hears the word of God, then convey him to his place of safety. That is because they are a people who do not know.

How can there be a compact for the associators with God and His Messenger — except those with whom you made a compact at the Sacred Mosque? So long as they go straight with you, go straight with them. God loves the God-fearing. How, when if they get the upper hand over you they do not observe any tie or compact with you? They please you with their mouths and their hearts refuse. Most of them are wicked. They sold God’s signs for a small price and barred from His path. Evil is what they did. They do not observe toward a believer any tie or compact. Those are the transgressors.

If they repent and establish the prayer and give the zakāt, they are your brothers in religion. We detail the signs for a people who know. If they break their oaths after their compact and taunt you in your religion, fight the leaders of unbelief. Their oaths are nothing. That they may refrain.

Will you not fight a people who broke their oaths and intended to expel the Messenger, and they began against you the first time? Do you fear them? God is worthier that you fear Him, if you are believers. Fight them. God will punish them by your hands and disgrace them and help you against them and heal the breasts of a people who believe, and remove the rage of their hearts. God turns to whom He wills. God is Knowing, Wise. Or did you think you would be left when God has not yet known those of you who strove and did not take other than God and His Messenger and the believers as intimates? God is aware of what you do.

1–3 bara'a; four months; announcement at the greater hajj. 4 exception: compact-keepers to term. 5 when sacred months pass: kill / take / besiege / ambush; repent+prayer+zakat = let go. 6 if a mushrik seeks jiwar, protect him until he hears, then convey to safety. 7–12 how can there be a compact; exception at the Sacred Mosque if they go straight; they observe no ill/dhimma; repent-prayer-zakat = brothers; if they break oaths fight leaders of kufr. 13–16 will you not fight those who broke and tried to expel the Messenger; God punishes by your hands; you will not be left untested.
Unique among 114. Later explanations (this is a war-writ; it continues 8; ʿAlī / Ibn ʿAbbās reports) are tafsīr. Level 1: the surah as written begins with bara'a, not with the name of the Merciful.

Bara'a from God and His Messenger toward those you contracted among the associators. Four months to travel. Announcement at the greater hajj. Exception: those who did not fail you and did not back anyone against you — fulfill to the term. The opening is not a blanket erasure of every compact. 8:58’s even-handed nabidh is the immediate cousin: throw back, then time.

When the sacred months have slipped: kill the associators wherever you find them; take, besiege, sit at every watch. Then: if they repent and establish prayer and give zakāt, let them go. God is Forgiving, Merciful. The verse is a time-bound command after a waiting period, aimed at al-mushrikīn in this compact-file, with a three-part off-ramp (repent, pray, zakāt). Later uses of 9:5 as a standing license against all non-Muslims forever are tafsīr-extension. Level 1 does not write ‘forever’ or ‘all religions.’ 9:6 sits immediately after: a seeking mushrik is protected until he hears the word, then conveyed home. Read 9:5 with 9:4 and 9:6, not alone.

How can there be compact — except those at the Sacred Mosque, so long as they go straight. They, if they get the upper hand, observe no tie (ill) or compact (dhimma) toward you or toward a believer. Repent + prayer + zakāt: brothers in religion. Break oaths after compact and taunt the religion: fight the aʾimmat al-kufr. Their oaths are nothing.

Will you not fight a people who broke oaths, intended to expel the Messenger, and began the first time? God will punish them by your hands, disgrace them, help you, heal believing breasts, remove rage. You will not be left until He knows who strove and did not take intimates besides God, the Messenger, and the believers.

bara'a. alladhīna ʿāhadtum mina l-mushrikīn. arbaʿata ashhur. yawm al-ḥajj al-akbar. insalakha l-ashhur al-ḥurum. fa-qtulū. fa-in tābu wa-aqāmū l-ṣalāta wa-ātaw l-zakāta. istajāra. fa-ajirhu. ill / dhimma. aʾimmat al-kufr. walīja.
SI: disassociation. Haleem: release. Pickthall: declaration of immunity. Arberry: acquittal.
bara'a = dissociation / being quit. Haleem's 'release' is legal. Pickthall's 'immunity' is older English.

SI: kill the polytheists wherever you find them. Haleem: kill the idolaters wherever you find them. Pickthall: slay the idolaters wherever ye find them. Arberry: slay the idolaters wherever you find them.
mushrikīn = associators / those who ascribe partners. 'Polytheists' / 'idolaters' are English choices. The off-ramp (repent, pray, zakat) is in the same verse.
9:5 khudhuhum wa-hsuruhum wa-q'udu lahum kulla marsad

SI: capture / besiege / sit in wait at every place of ambush. Haleem: capture, besiege, lie in wait. Pickthall: take them, besiege them, prepare for them each ambush. Arberry: take them, and confine them, and lie in wait for them at every place of ambush.
Four verbs: kill, take, confine, sit-watch.

SI: seeks your protection / grant him protection / his place of safety. Haleem: seeks your protection / give it / place of safety. Pickthall: seeketh thy protection / give him / place of safety. Arberry: seeks thy protection / grant him / place of security.
No split that softens 9:5's neighbor verse.
SI: kinship or treaty of protection. Haleem: tie of kinship or treaty. Pickthall: pact nor honour. Arberry: pact nor bond.
Two words for bond. SI/Haleem split kinship vs treaty. Keep both Arabic.
Yusuf Ali 9:5 line only: 'fight and slay the Pagans wherever ye find them.' 'Pagans' is his word.

God and the Messenger jointly issue bara'a. Compacts kept to the term are still honored. After sacred months: four verbs of war against the associators of this file, with a ritual off-ramp. A seeking mushrik is walked to safety after hearing. Compact-breakers who began and tried to expel the Messenger are the people 9:13 names. Brotherhood in religion is defined here as repent + prayer + zakāt.

8:58 nabidh on even terms — walked last packet. 2:190–193 / 8:39 fight-until — walked. 9:29 People of the Book jizya is the next major parked cousin (coming in this surah). Deut 20; Exod 23:31–33 / Deut 7:2 no covenant with certain nations. QB-0248 PARTIAL AGREEMENT with 8:58’s public end of compact. QB-0249 CONTRAST of 9:5’s after-term kill-order with 8:61 incline-to-peace — both now walked; do not let one eat the other without a later naskh argument labeled as such. QB-0250 OPEN: scope of al-mushrikīn in 9:5 (this compact-set vs all associators everywhere for all time).
No basmala; opens with bara'a from God and His Messenger
Four months; announcement at greater hajj; keep compact to term if they kept it
9:5 after sacred months: kill / take / besiege / ambush; off-ramp repent-pray-zakat
9:6 seeking mushrik is protected, hears, conveyed to safety
How a compact; ill and dhimma; brothers if repent-pray-zakat; fight a'immat al-kufr if they break
Fight those who broke, tried to expel the Messenger, began first; punish by your hands
9:5 and 8:61 both walked — do not naskh silently
A written quit-claim, a four-month window, an honored exception, then 9:5 with 9:6 beside it. Next: 9:17–37 — mosque, Abraham, jizya, sacred months delayed.

packets.title: S009 Al-Tawba CP02 vv017-028
paragraphs: Hold: 9:29 jizya begins the next packet on purpose.

It is not for the associators to maintain God’s mosques while they witness against themselves with unbelief. Those — their works are vain. In the Fire they abide. God’s mosques are maintained only by one who believes in God and the Last Day, establishes the prayer, gives the zakāt, and fears none but God. It may be that those are among the guided.

Do you count the giving of water to the pilgrim and the maintaining of the Sacred Mosque as equal to one who believes in God and the Last Day and strives in God’s path? They are not equal with God. God does not guide the wrongdoing people. Those who believed and emigrated and strove in God’s path with their property and their lives are greater in degree with God. Those are the triumphant. Their Lord gives them good news of mercy from Him, and pleasure, and gardens in which for them is lasting bliss, abiding there forever. God has with Him a great wage.

O you who believe, do not take your fathers and your brothers as awliyāʾ if they prefer unbelief to belief. Whoever of you takes them as such — those are the wrongdoers. Say: if your fathers, your sons, your brothers, your spouses, your clan, the wealth you have acquired, a trade you fear slump in, and dwellings you are pleased with are dearer to you than God and His Messenger and striving in His path, then wait until God comes with His command. God does not guide the wicked people.

God has already helped you on many fields, and on the day of Ḥunayn when your great number pleased you and it availed you nothing, and the land was strait for you with all its breadth, then you turned back retreating. Then God sent down His sakīna on His Messenger and on the believers, and sent down forces you did not see, and punished those who disbelieved. That is the recompense of the unbelievers. Then God turns after that to whom He wills. God is Forgiving, Merciful.

O you who believe, the associators are only najas, so let them not come near the Sacred Mosque after this year of theirs. If you fear poverty, God will enrich you from His bounty if He wills. God is Knowing, Wise.

17–18 who may maintain mosques. 19–22 watering pilgrims ≠ belief-plus-jihād; emigrants who strove have the higher degree. 23–24 no awliyāʾ from fathers/brothers if they prefer kufr; a list of dear things that must not outrank God, Messenger, and jihād. 25–27 Ḥunayn: numbers failed; sakīna and unseen forces; then He turns. 28 mushrikūn are najas; keep them from the Sacred Mosque after this year; fear of poverty answered by bounty.

Associators may not ʿamara God’s mosques while they witness unbelief against themselves. Works vain; Fire. Maintainers: believe, Last Day, prayer, zakāt, fear none but God. Giving water to ḥajj pilgrims and keeping the Sacred Mosque is named as a rival boast — and declared not equal to belief-plus-jihād. Level 1 is a ranking of deeds, not a travelogue.

Fathers and brothers are not awliyāʾ if they prefer unbelief. Then a longer list: fathers, sons, brothers, spouses, clan, acquired wealth, a trade you fear will slump, pleasing dwellings — if these are dearer than God, His Messenger, and striving in His path, wait for God’s command. The Messenger is again in the triad of what must outrank kin and property (cousin of 8:24 and of 9:16’s no intimates besides God/Messenger/believers).

First time this surah names a battle. Your multitude pleased you and did not avail. Land became strait; you turned back. Then sakīna on the Messenger and the believers; forces you did not see; punishment of the unbelievers; then tawba toward whom He wills. Numbers are not the help. 8:9–12’s unseen help is the cousin.

The associators are only najas (unclean / defilement). They are not to come near the Sacred Mosque after this year of theirs. Fear of poverty (lost pilgrimage trade) — God will enrich from His bounty if He wills. Najas here is a legal-status word tied to mosque access, not a biology lesson. How far it runs beyond the Sacred Mosque is not stated in this verse.
yaʿmura masājid Allāh. siqāyat al-ḥājj. aʿẓamu darajatan. awliyāʾ. ʿashīra. tijāra. masākin. yawm Ḥunayn. sakīna. najas. ʿām hādhā.
SI: maintain. Haleem: tend. Pickthall: tend. Arberry: inhabit / inhabit God's places of worship.
ʿamara = inhabit / tend / keep alive. Arberry hears inhabit.
SI: providing water. Haleem: giving water. Pickthall: giving drink. Arberry: giving drink.
A known Meccan prestige-office. Ranked below jihad.
Rare: a battle named in the verse itself (unlike Badr in S008).
SI: tranquillity. Haleem: calm. Pickthall: peace of reassurance. Arberry: Shechina / reassurance.
Arberry's Shechina flags the cousin-word. Keep sakina.
SI: unclean. Haleem: filth. Pickthall: unclean. Arberry: unclean.
Status-word for mosque-approach after this year. Haleem's 'filth' is harsher English.
Yusuf Ali 9:28 line only: 'The Pagans are unclean.'

Mosque-tending without tawḥīd is vain. Watering pilgrims is not the equal of belief-plus-jihād. Kin who prefer kufr are not awliyāʾ. A list of ordinary loves must not outrank God, Messenger, and path-striving. Multitude failed at a named battle; sakīna and unseen forces did not. Associators barred from the Sacred Mosque after this year because they are najas; lost trade is answered by bounty, not by keeping them at the House.

8:72 walāya of emigrants. 9:16 walīja. 2:191 Sacred Mosque fight-exception already walked. Temple / ger access in Torah is a cousin of holy-space restriction (Deut 23:1–8 foreigner lists — different logic). QB-0251 RANKING: siqāya < īmān+jihād. QB-0252 Ḥunayn named; Badr in S008 was not. QB-0253 najas-bar on the Sacred Mosque after this year — scope beyond that House OPEN.
Associators may not maintain God's mosques; works vain
Watering pilgrims not equal to belief plus jihad
Emigrants who strove: greater degree, triumph, gardens
No awliya' of kin who prefer kufr; dear-list vs God-Messenger-jihad
Hunayn: numbers failed; sakina and unseen forces
Mushrikun najas; not near Sacred Mosque after this year
Hunayn named in-verse; Badr was not
Najas-bar scope beyond the House OPEN
9:29–37 — fight those given the Book until jizya; Uzayr / Messiah-as-son; rabbis and monks; twelve months and nasīʾ.

packets.title: S009 Al-Tawba CP03 vv029-037
paragraphs: Fight those who do not believe in God or in the Last Day, and do not forbid what God and His Messenger have forbidden, and do not profess the religion of truth — from those who were given the Book — until they give the jizya from a hand while they are ṣāghirūn.

The Jews said ʿUzayr is the son of God. The Christians said the Messiah is the son of God. That is their saying with their mouths. They imitate the saying of those who disbelieved before. God fight them. How they are turned. They took their rabbis and their monks as lords besides God, and the Messiah son of Mary. They were not commanded except to worship one God. There is no god but He. Glory to Him above what they associate.

They want to extinguish God’s light with their mouths. God refuses except to perfect His light, even if the unbelievers dislike it. He is the one who sent His Messenger with the guidance and the religion of truth to make it prevail over the religion, all of it, even if the associators dislike it.

O you who believe, many of the rabbis and monks devour the wealth of the people in vanity and bar from God’s path. Those who hoard gold and silver and do not spend it in God’s path — give them news of a painful punishment on the day it is heated in the fire of Hell and their foreheads and sides and backs are branded with it: this is what you hoarded for yourselves. Taste what you used to hoard.

The number of months with God is twelve months in God’s Book the day He created the heavens and the earth. Of them four are sacred. That is the right religion. Do not wrong yourselves in them. Fight the associators all together as they fight you all together. Know that God is with the God-fearing. The nasīʾ is only an increase in unbelief by which those who disbelieve are led astray. They make it lawful one year and forbidden one year to match the number of what God made sacred, so they make lawful what God made forbidden. Their evil deeds are made fair to them. God does not guide the unbelieving people.

29 fight People of the Book under three negatives, until jizya from a hand while saghirun. 30–31 ʿUzayr-as-son; Messiah-as-son; rabbis and monks as lords; Messiah son of Mary; only command was one God. 32–33 mouths vs light; Messenger sent to make din al-haqq prevail over the religion all of it. 34–35 many rabbis/monks devour wealth; hoarded gold and silver branded. 36–37 twelve months, four sacred; fight associators collectively as they fight you; nasi' is extra kufr.

Addressees: those given the Book who (a) do not believe in God or the Last Day, (b) do not forbid what God and His Messenger forbade, (c) do not profess din al-ḥaqq. Until: they give jizya ʿan yadin wa-hum ṣāghirūn. This is not 9:5. Different target-set (Book-people, not mushrikūn of the compact-file). Different end-state (jizya while low, not repent-pray-zakāt). Do not flatten 9:5 and 9:29 into one sword.

Jews said ʿUzayr is ibn Allāh. Christians said the Messiah is ibn Allāh. Mouth-saying; imitation of earlier unbelievers. ʿUzayr is the Quran’s name usually mapped to Ezra. Mainstream rabbinic Judaism does not call Ezra son of God. The verse states that some Jews said it. It does not locate the synagogue. Messiah-as-son is the walked Christian claim already in S004–S005 Christology file. Qātalahumu llāh is invective, not a battle-order in this sentence.

Rabbis and monks taken as lords besides God, and the Messiah son of Mary. They were commanded only to worship one God. Taking scholars as arbāb is paired with taking the Messiah as lord. Christology dossier add: Messiah son of Mary, not son of God, in the same breath as the rebuke.

Messenger sent with guidance and din al-ḥaqq to make it prevail over the religion, all of it (li-yuẓhirahu ʿalā l-dīni kullihi). Cousin of 8:39’s religion all God’s. Scope of ‘all of it’ is a later legal question. Level 1 is a prevail-clause.

Twelve months in God’s Book the day He created heaven and earth. Four sacred. Fight the associators all together as they fight you all together. Nasīʾ (intercalary postponement of a sacred month) is extra unbelief: they make lawful what God forbade to keep the count. Calendar-manipulation is named as kufr-increase.
alladhīna ūtū l-kitāb. jizya. ʿan yadin. ṣāghirūn. ʿUzayr. al-Masīḥ. aḥbār / ruhbān. arbāb. yuẓhirahu ʿalā l-dīni kullihi. ithnā ʿashara shahran. nasīʾ.
9:29 hatta yu'tu l-jizyata 'an yadin wa-hum saghirun

SI: until they give the jizyah willingly while they are humbled. Haleem: until they pay the tax and agree to submit. Pickthall: until they pay the tribute readily, being brought low. Arberry: until they pay the tribute out of hand and have been humbled.

ʿan yadin: from a hand / readily / out of hand. ṣāghirūn: humbled / brought low / submit. SI's 'willingly' is a gloss of ʿan yadin. Haleem's 'agree to submit' folds saghirun into a treaty-tone. Keep both phrases.
SI: Uzair. Haleem: Ezra. Pickthall: Ezra. Arberry: Ezra.
Haleem/Pickthall/Arberry identify. SI transliterates. Identification is standard and still a mapping.
SI: May Allah destroy them. Haleem: God confound them. Pickthall: Allah's curse be on them. Arberry: God assail them.
SI: over all religion. Haleem: over all religions. Pickthall: over all religion. Arberry: over every religion.
al-din kullihi: the religion, all of it / every religion. Haleem/Arberry hear plurality of religions.
SI: postponing [of restriction]. Haleem: postponing sacred months. Pickthall: postponement [of a sacred month]. Arberry: the month postponed.
Intercalation / shifting a sacred month. Named as increase in kufr.
Yusuf Ali 9:29 line only: 'until they pay the Jizya with willing submission, and feel themselves subdued.'

Book-people who fail three tests are fought until jizya from a hand while low — a subordinate-pay end-state, not the 9:5 off-ramp. A Jewish ʿUzayr-as-son saying is asserted; a Christian Messiah-as-son saying is restated. Scholars-as-lords is shirk-shaped. The Messenger is sent so din al-ḥaqq prevails over the religion entire. Hoarded metal is branded. The calendar is God’s from creation; moving a sacred month is extra unbelief. Fight associators collectively as they fight you collectively.

Christology file: 4:171, 5:17, 5:72–75, 5:116. 8:39 din kulluhu lillāh. Tribute-cousins: 2 Sam 8; 2 Kgs 17; NT tax (Matt 22:21) is not jizya. Ezra in Jewish canon is scribe, not son (Ezra 7). QB-0254 CONTRAST 9:5 vs 9:29 (target and end-state differ). QB-0255 CONTRAST ʿUzayr-as-son vs pre-Islamic Jewish text as we have it. QB-0256 AGREEMENT of target on Christian ‘son’ claim. QB-0257 Prevail-clause cousin of 8:39.
Fight Book-people under three negatives until jizya from a hand while saghirun
Jews said Uzayr is son of God; Christians said the Messiah is son of God
Rabbis and monks taken as lords; Messiah son of Mary; only one God commanded
Light perfected; Messenger sent to make din al-haqq prevail over the religion all of it
Many rabbis/monks devour wealth; hoarded gold and silver branded
Twelve months four sacred; nasi' is increase in kufr
Messiah-as-son AGREEMENT of target with walked Christology
9:38–59 — go forth, Tabūk-tone, hypocrites who stay behind, sadaqa mockers.

packets.title: S009 Al-Tawba CP04 vv038-052
paragraphs: O you who believe, what is with you that when you are told go forth in God’s path you cling heavily to the earth? Are you pleased with this world’s life instead of the last? The enjoyment of this world’s life is only little in the last. If you do not go forth He will punish you a painful punishment and replace you with another people. You will not harm Him anything. God is over all things powerful.

If you do not help him — God already helped him when those who disbelieved expelled him, the second of two, when they were in the cave, when he said to his companion: do not grieve, God is with us. God sent down His sakīna on him and supported him with forces you did not see, and made the word of those who disbelieved the lowest, and God’s word is the highest. God is Mighty, Wise.

Go forth light and heavy, and strive with your property and your lives in God’s path. That is better for you if you knew. Had it been a near gain and a short journey they would have followed you, but the distance was far for them. They will swear by God: if we could we would have gone out with you. They destroy themselves. God knows they are liars.

God pardon you. Why did you give them leave before it became clear to you who were truthful and you knew the liars? Those who believe in God and the Last Day do not ask your leave to strive with their property and their lives. God knows the God-fearing. Only those who do not believe in God and the Last Day ask your leave, their hearts in doubt, tossing in their doubt.

Had they wanted to go forth they would have prepared some preparation for it. But God disliked their being sent forth, so He made them lag, and it was said: sit with the sitters. Had they gone out among you they would have increased you only in ruin and hurried about in your midst seeking fitna for you. Among you are listeners to them. God knows the wrongdoers. They sought fitna before and turned matters over for you until the truth came and God’s command appeared, while they were averse.

Among them is he who says: give me leave and do not tempt me. In the fitna they have fallen. Hell encompasses the unbelievers. If good meets you it vexes them. If a hit meets you they say: we took our matter before, and they turn away rejoicing. Say: nothing meets us except what God wrote for us. He is our mawlā. On God let the believers rely. Say: do you await for us except one of the two best things? We await for you that God will hit you with a punishment from Him or by our hands. So wait. We are waiting with you.

38–39 cling to earth; go forth or be replaced. 40 cave: the second of two; sakina; unseen forces; God’s word highest. 41 go light and heavy; property and lives. 42 far journey; they swear. 43–45 pardon you for giving leave; believers do not ask leave; doubters do. 46–48 God made them lag; they would have been ruin and fitna. 49–52 ‘do not tempt me’; good vexes them; two best things.

Told to go forth in God’s path, they cling to the earth. This world’s enjoyment is little in the last. If you do not go: painful punishment, replacement by another people. The command is mobilization, not a proverb.

If you do not help him — God already helped him when they expelled him, the second of two, in the cave: do not grieve, God is with us. Sakīna on him; unseen forces; the unbelievers’ word made lowest; God’s word highest. Traditional hijra-cave with Abū Bakr. Level 1: a second person, a cave, grief forbidden, God with ‘us.’ The companion is not named.

Go light and heavy (young/old, armed/unarmed — later glosses; Arabic is light and heavy). Strive with property and lives. Near gain they would have followed; the distance was far. They swear they would have gone. God pardon you — why give them leave before the truthful and the liars were clear? Believers do not ask leave to strive. Doubters do. God disliked their going, made them lag: sit with the sitters. Had they gone they would have been ruin and fitna. Listeners to them are among you.

Give me leave, do not tempt me (fitna). They have already fallen into it. Good that meets you vexes them; a hit and they say we took our affair beforehand. Nothing meets us except what God wrote. Two best things await us (later: victory or martyrdom). We await for you a punishment from Him or by our hands.
infirū. iththāqaltum ilā l-arḍ. thaniya ithnayn. al-ghār. lā taḥzan. khifāfan wa-thiqālan. ʿadhara. qʿudū maʿa l-qāʿidīn. iḥdā l-ḥusnayayn.
SI: cling heavily to the earth. Haleem: cling heavily to the ground. Pickthall: cling to the earth. Arberry: sink down heavily to the ground.

SI: the second of two when they were in the cave. Haleem: the second of two in the cave. Pickthall: the second of two; when they two were in the cave. Arberry: the second of two, when the two were in the cave.
SI: light or heavy. Haleem: whether lightly or heavily armed. Pickthall: light-armed and heavy-armed. Arberry: light and heavy.
Haleem/Pickthall hear armament. SI/Arberry keep light/heavy.
SI: May Allah pardon you. Haleem: God forgive you. Pickthall: Allah forgive thee. Arberry: God pardon thee.
Addressed to the Prophet for giving leave too soon.
SI: one of the two best things. Haleem: one of two excellent outcomes. Pickthall: one of two good things. Arberry: one of the two rewards most fair.
The two are not named in the verse. Later: victory or death in the path.
Yusuf Ali 9:40 line only: 'the second of two, when they two were in the cave.'

Refusal to go forth is clinging to the earth and risks replacement. Help of the Messenger is not required for God to have already helped him — cave, sakīna, unseen forces, His word highest. Asking leave to stay is a mark of doubt, not of belief. Giving that leave too soon is pardoned and still corrected. Fitna-seekers among the stay-behinds would have been ruin inside the column. What meets the believers is only what was written; they await one of two goods; the other side awaits a blow from God or from their hands.

8:30 plot to expel. 9:13 intended to expel. 9:26 sakīna at Ḥunayn. Cave-help has no Torah twin. QB-0258 cave-help as hijra-memory (companion unnamed). QB-0259 replacement-threat if they will not go forth.
Go forth; clinging to earth; replaced if you do not
Cave: second of two; do not grieve; sakina; God's word highest
Go light and heavy; strive with property and lives
Pardon for giving leave too soon; believers do not ask leave
God made the doubtful lag; they would have been fitna inside
Two best things for us; a blow from Him or our hands for you
Replacement if they will not mobilize
9:53–74 — spend, hypocrites’ mockery of ṣadaqāt, they are the enemy, promise of Fire.

packets.title: S009 Al-Tawba CP05 vv053-066
paragraphs: Say: spend willingly or unwillingly; it will not be accepted from you. You have been a wicked people. What prevents their spendings being accepted from them except that they have disbelieved in God and in His Messenger, and they do not come to prayer except lazily, and they do not spend except unwillingly. So let not their wealth or their children impress you. God only wants to punish them with those in this world’s life, and that their souls should depart while they are unbelievers.

They swear by God they are of you. They are not of you. They are a people who are afraid. If they found a refuge or caves or a place to enter they would turn to it rushing. Among them is he who finds fault with you about the ṣadaqāt. If they are given from them they are pleased. If they are not given from them they are angry. If they had been pleased with what God and His Messenger gave them and said: God is sufficient for us; God will give us of His bounty, and His Messenger; toward God we turn —.

The ṣadaqāt are only for the poor, the needy, those who work over them, those whose hearts are brought together, for necks, the debt-burdened, in God’s path, and the son of the road — a duty from God. God is Knowing, Wise.

Among them are those who hurt the Prophet and say: he is an ear. Say: an ear of good for you. He believes in God and believes the believers, and is a mercy to those of you who believe. Those who hurt the Messenger of God — for them a painful punishment. They swear by God to you to please you. God and His Messenger are worthier that they should please Him if they are believers. Do they not know that whoever opposes God and His Messenger — for him the fire of Hell, abiding in it? That is the great disgrace.

The hypocrites are afraid that a sūra will be sent down about them telling them what is in their hearts. Say: mock. God will bring out what you caution against. If you ask them they will say: we were only talking and playing. Say: were you mocking God and His signs and His Messenger? Do not make excuse. You have disbelieved after your belief. If We pardon a party of you We will punish a party, because they have been criminals.

53–55 spend not accepted; lazy prayer; wealth and children as punishment-instrument. 56–57 they swear they are of you; they would bolt to a refuge. 58–59 they fault the Prophet over ṣadaqāt; pleased only when given. 60 eight heads of ṣadaqāt. 61–63 they hurt him: he is an ear; opposing God and His Messenger. 64–66 they fear a sūra; we were only playing; disbelief after belief; a party pardoned, a party punished.

Willing or unwilling, spending is not accepted: they disbelieved in God and His Messenger, come to prayer lazily, spend unwillingly. Wealth and children: do not be impressed; He wants to punish them by means of those and that they die unbelieving. They swear they are of you. They are not. They are afraid. A refuge, caves, an entrance — they would rush to it.

They fault him about the ṣadaqāt: given, pleased; not given, angry. Counterfactual: if they had been pleased with what God and His Messenger gave. Then 9:60 lists eight: fuqarāʾ, masākīn, ʿāmilīna ʿalayhā, muʾallafati qulūbuhum, fī l-riqāb, ghārimīn, fī sabīli llāh, ibn al-sabīl — farīḍatan mina llāh. This is the walked statutory list for ṣadaqāt. Later fiqh maps zakāt onto it. Level 1 is the eight and ‘a duty from God.’

They hurt the Prophet: he is an ear (udhun — he listens to anyone). Reply: an ear of good for you. He believes in God and believes the believers, a mercy to those who believe. Those who hurt the Messenger: painful punishment. They swear to please you. God and His Messenger are worthier to be pleased. Opposing God and His Messenger: Hell, abiding, great disgrace. Messenger-hurt is named as its own crime.

Hypocrites fear a sūra exposing what is in their hearts. Mock: He will bring out what you caution. We were only conversing and playing. Were you mocking God, His signs, and His Messenger? Do not excuse. You have disbelieved after your belief. A party pardoned; a party punished as criminals. Disbelief after belief is walked here as the verdict on that mockery.
anfiqū ṭawʿan aw karhan. kusālā. yalmizuka fī l-ṣadaqāt. fuqarāʾ / masākīn / ʿāmilīn / muʾallafa / riqāb / ghārimīn / sabīl Allāh / ibn al-sabīl. udhun. yuʾdhūna l-nabiyy. kafartum baʿda īmānikum.

SI: poor, needy, those employed to collect, whose hearts are brought together, for freeing slaves, those in debt, in the way of Allah, the traveler. Haleem: poor, needy, those who administer them, whose hearts are to be won over, to free slaves, those in debt, God's cause, travellers. Pickthall: poor, needy, those who collect, those whose hearts are to be reconciled, to free captives, debtors, way of Allah, wayfarer. Arberry: poor, needy, who work to collect them, whose hearts are brought together, slaves, debtors, in God's way, the traveller.
riqab = necks (slaves/captives). mu'allafa qulubuhum = whose hearts are brought together / reconciled / won. Keep the eight Arabic heads.
SI: He is an ear. Haleem: He listens to anyone. Pickthall: He is only a hearer. Arberry: He is an ear.
Insult: credulous listener. Reply: ear of good.
SI: conversing and playing. Haleem: only talking idly and joking. Pickthall: discoursing and jesting. Arberry: only talking idly and making jest.
Idle talk as the excuse for mocking God, signs, Messenger.
SI: You have disbelieved after your belief. Haleem: You have turned from belief to disbelief. Pickthall: Ye have disbelieved after your belief. Arberry: you have disbelieved after your believing.
After-belief kufr. Not a first refusal.
Yusuf Ali 9:60 line only: eight classes matching SI closely; 'those whose hearts have been recently reconciled.'

Spending from hypocrites is rejected even when performed. Prayer can be present and lazy. Ṣadaqāt have eight named heads, a duty from God. Faulting the Messenger over distribution is a mark of that party. Calling him an ear is hurting him. Mocking a feared sūra is disbelief after belief. A party of them may be pardoned; a party punished.

2:264 charity with reminder/injury. 2:215 / 2:273 spend-categories earlier, not this eight. Lev 27 / Num 18 tithe-cousins are not this list. QB-0263 eight-head ṣadaqāt list is unique in walked text. QB-0264 hurting the Messenger named as its own crime. QB-0265 kufr after īmān on mockery of God/signs/Messenger.
Spend willing or not: not accepted; lazy prayer; wealth as punishment-instrument
They swear they are of you; they are afraid; would bolt to a refuge
They fault him over sadaqat; pleased only when given
Eight heads of sadaqat; a duty from God
He is an ear; hurting the Messenger; oppose God and His Messenger
Fear a sura; mockery is disbelief after belief; party pardoned, party punished
Hurting the Messenger as named crime
9:67–89 — hypocrites male and female; they bid the wrong; fight the hypocrites; Bedouin stay-behinds; those who were true.

packets.title: S009 Al-Tawba CP06 vv067-080
paragraphs: The hypocrite men and the hypocrite women are of one another. They bid the wrong and forbid the right, and they close their hands. They have forgotten God so He has forgotten them. The hypocrites — they are the wicked. God has promised the hypocrite men and the hypocrite women and the unbelievers the fire of Hell, abiding in it. It is enough for them. God has cursed them. For them a lasting punishment.

Like those before you. They were stronger than you in power and more in wealth and children. They enjoyed their portion. You have enjoyed your portion as those before you enjoyed their portion. You have plunged as they plunged. Those — their works are vain in this world and the next. Those are the losers. Has there not come to them the news of those before them — the people of Noah, and ʿĀd, and Thamūd, and the people of Abraham, and the companions of Midian, and the overturned towns? Their messengers came to them with the clear signs. God was not to wrong them, but they wronged themselves.

The believing men and the believing women are awliyāʾ of one another. They bid the right and forbid the wrong, establish the prayer, give the zakāt, and obey God and His Messenger. Those — God will have mercy on them. God is Mighty, Wise. God has promised the believing men and the believing women gardens under which rivers flow, abiding in them, and good dwellings in gardens of Eden. And pleasure from God is greater. That is the great triumph.

O Prophet, fight the unbelievers and the hypocrites, and be harsh with them. Their refuge is Hell. Wretched destination. They swear by God they said nothing. They have said the word of unbelief, and disbelieved after their submission, and intended what they did not attain. They did not take revenge except that God and His Messenger enriched them from His bounty. If they repent it is better for them. If they turn away God will punish them a painful punishment in this world and the next. They have in the earth no friend or helper.

Among them are those who made a compact with God: if He gives us of His bounty we will give ṣadaqa and be of the righteous. When He gave them of His bounty they were stingy with it and turned away, averse. He placed hypocrisy in their hearts until the day they meet Him, because they broke God in what they promised Him and because they used to lie. Did they not know that God knows their secret and their private talk, and that God is the knower of the hidden things?

Those who find fault with the believers who give ṣadaqāt freely, and with those who find nothing to give but their effort — they mock them. God mocks them. For them a painful punishment. Ask forgiveness for them or do not ask forgiveness for them. If you ask forgiveness for them seventy times, God will not forgive them. That is because they have disbelieved in God and His Messenger. God does not guide the wicked people.

67–68 hypocrites male/female of one another; bid wrong; closed hands; Fire promised with the unbelievers. 69–70 like those before; Noah, ʿĀd, Thamūd, Abraham’s people, Midian, overturned towns. 71–72 believing men/women as mutual awliyāʾ; opposite ethic; gardens and God’s pleasure greater. 73 fight unbelievers and hypocrites; be harsh. 74 they swore they said nothing; word of kufr after islām; intended what they did not attain; enriched then ungrateful. 75–78 bounty-vow broken; hypocrisy placed in hearts. 79 mock the givers, even those who give only effort. 80 ask forgiveness or not — seventy times will not forgive.

Hypocrite men and women are of one another: bid munkar, forbid maʿrūf, close the hand, forgot God. Believing men and women are awliyāʾ of one another: bid maʿrūf, forbid munkar, pray, zakāt, obey God and His Messenger. The pair is ethical and sexed. God’s pleasure is named greater than the gardens.

O Prophet, fight the unbelievers and the hypocrites, and be harsh with them. Hell is their refuge. Jāhid here includes the hypocrites in the fight-command. How that fight looks (sword vs severity of treatment) is later fiqh. Level 1: both classes named as objects of the Prophet’s jihād and ghilẓa.

They swear they said nothing. They said kalimat al-kufr and disbelieved after their islām, and intended what they did not reach. Revenge-motive denied: they were enriched by God and His Messenger. Repent: better. Turn away: punishment here and next, no walī or naṣīr in the land.

Ask forgiveness for them or do not. If you ask seventy times, God will not forgive them. They have disbelieved in God and His Messenger. The Messenger’s intercession-request is here capped and refused for this class. Cousin of 9:113 (coming) — do not ask for the associators, even kin.
al-munāfiqūn wa-l-munāfiqāt. yaʾmurūna bi-l-munkar. yaqbiḍūna aydiyahum. al-muʾminūn wa-l-muʾmināt baʿḍuhum awliyāʾ baʿḍ. jāhid / ghluẓ. kalimat al-kufr. baʿda islāmihim. sabʿīna marratan.
SI: are of one another. Haleem: are all the same. Pickthall: are as one. Arberry: are as one another.
Of one stock / of each other. Shared ethic.
SI: fight ... and be harsh. Haleem: strive against ... and be tough. Pickthall: strive against ... and be stern. Arberry: struggle with ... and be thou harsh.
Jahid + ghilza. Haleem's 'strive' is softer English than SI 'fight.' Same verb family as 9:41.
SI: after their [pretending to] Islam. Haleem: after having professed Islam. Pickthall: after their acceptance of Islam. Arberry: after they accepted Islam.
SI inserts 'pretending.' The Arabic is after their islam.
SI: seventy times. Haleem: seventy times. Pickthall: seventy times. Arberry: seventy times.
No split. Forgiveness refused even at seventy.
Yusuf Ali 9:80 line only: 'Whether thou ask for their forgiveness, or not... seventy times...'

Hypocrisy is a two-gender collective with an inverted command-ethic (bid wrong, forbid right, closed hand). Belief is the mirrored collective. The Prophet is told to fight unbelievers and hypocrites and be harsh. Kufr after islām is named again (after 9:66’s after-īmān). A broken bounty-vow becomes hypocrisy placed in the heart until they meet Him. Mocking small givers is mocked back. Seventy petitions will not forgive this class.

3:167 hypocrites already walked. 4:145 hypocrites in the lowest depth — walked. 9:66 kufr after īmān. 9:113 parked. Noah/ʿĀd/Thamūd/Midian already in S007. QB-0266 sexed pair of hypocrites vs sexed pair of believers. QB-0267 jihād-command includes hypocrites. QB-0268 seventy-forgiveness cap.
Hypocrite men and women of one another; bid wrong; closed hands
Believing men and women awliya' of one another; opposite ethic; God's pleasure greater
Fight unbelievers and hypocrites; be harsh
They said the word of kufr after their islam; intended what they did not attain
Bounty-vow broken; hypocrisy placed in hearts
Mock the givers; seventy askings will not forgive
9:81–99 — stay-behinds glad of sitting; desert Arabs; those who confess fault; Bedouin hypocrites and Bedouin believers.

packets.title: S009 Al-Tawba CP07 vv081-089
paragraphs: Note: 7:203 confirmed as the no-manufactured-sign verse on the authority frame.

Those who were left behind rejoiced at their sitting contrary to the Messenger of God, and disliked to strive with their property and their lives in God’s path. They said: do not go forth in the heat. Say: the fire of Hell is hotter, if they would understand. So let them laugh a little and weep much, a recompense for what they have been earning.

If God returns you to a party of them and they ask your leave to go forth, say: you will never go forth with me, and you will never fight an enemy with me. You were pleased with sitting the first time, so sit with those who stay behind.
Do not pray over any of them who dies, ever, and do not stand at his grave. They disbelieved in God and His Messenger and died while they were wicked.
Do not let their wealth and their children impress you. God only wants to punish them with those in this world, and that their souls depart while they are unbelievers.

When a sūra is sent down: believe in God and strive with His Messenger, those of them with means ask your leave and say: leave us to be with the sitters. They were pleased to be with those who stay behind. Their hearts were sealed, so they do not understand.

But the Messenger and those who believed with him strove with their property and their lives. Those — for them the good things. Those are the successful. God has prepared for them gardens under which rivers flow, abiding in them. That is the great triumph.

81–82 glad to sit; heat-excuse; Hell hotter; laugh little weep much. 83 if you return, they will never go forth with you again. 84 no funeral prayer, no grave-stand. 85 wealth/children again as punishment-instrument. 86–87 a sūra to believe and strive; the well-off ask leave; hearts sealed. 88–89 the Messenger and those who believed with him did strive; gardens.

Left behind (khullifū) rejoiced at sitting khilāfa rasūli llāh — contrary to / behind the Messenger of God. Disliked striving with property and lives. Heat-excuse. Hell is hotter. If God returns you to a party of them and they ask leave to go out: never with me, never fight an enemy with me. First sitting binds the second. The Messenger is told the sentence to say.

Do not pray over any of them who dies, ever. Do not stand at his grave. They disbelieved in God and His Messenger and died as wicked. This is a ritual bar added to 9:80’s forgiveness-cap. The Prophet’s funeral-prayer and grave-stand are withdrawn from this class.

When a sūra says believe and strive with His Messenger, the well-off ask leave: let us be with the sitters. Hearts sealed. The Messenger and those who believed with him strove with property and lives. Good things; success; gardens. The split is not ‘Muslim / non-Muslim’ on the page. It is those who go with him versus those who sit contrary to him.
khullifū. qaʿadū khilāfa rasūli llāh. al-ḥarr. nār jahannam ashadd ḥarran. lā tuṣalli ʿalā aḥadin minhum māta abadan. lā taqum ʿalā qabrihi. dhawū l-ṭawl. ṭabaʿa Allāhu ʿalā qulūbihim.
SI: remaining behind [in disobedience to] the Messenger. Haleem: staying behind the Messenger. Pickthall: sitting still behind the messenger. Arberry: sitting at home behind God's Messenger.
khilafa = behind / contrary to. Disobedience is SI's gloss.

SI: do not pray [funeral] over any of them who dies, ever, or stand at his grave. Haleem: do not hold funeral prayers for any of them... or stand at their graves. Pickthall: pray not... nor stand by his grave. Arberry: do not pray over any one of them when he is dead, nor stand by his tomb.
Two acts barred: salat over the dead, standing at the grave.
SI: those who possess wealth. Haleem: those with the means. Pickthall: those who possess wealth. Arberry: those of them who possess bounty.
tawl = means / bounty / length. The well-off asking leave is the sting.
Yusuf Ali 9:84 line only: 'Nor do thou ever pray for any of them that dies, nor stand at his grave.'

Sitting contrary to the Messenger is named as the stay-behinds’ joy. Heat is answered with Hell. A second expedition with him is closed to that party. Funeral prayer and grave-stand are withdrawn. Wealth still does not impress. A sūra that says ‘strive with His Messenger’ exposes the well-off sitters. The successful column is the Messenger plus those who believed with him and actually went.

9:80 seventy-cap. 9:113 parked (no ask for associator-kin). 8:72 hijra-walāya. QB-0270 funeral-bar as ritual extension of the forgiveness-cap. QB-0271 ‘with the Messenger’ vs ‘behind the Messenger’ as this surah’s split.
Stay-behinds rejoiced at sitting contrary to the Messenger; heat-excuse; Hell hotter
They will never go forth or fight with him again
No funeral prayer, no grave-stand, ever
Sura to strive with the Messenger; well-off ask leave; hearts sealed
The Messenger and those who believed with him strove; gardens
With him / behind him as this surah's split
9:90–110 — desert Arabs; those who confess mixed deeds; deferred cases; the harm-mosque.

packets.title: S009 Al-Tawba CP08 vv090-099
paragraphs: The desert-Arabs came with excuses, that leave be given them, and those who lied to God and His Messenger sat. A painful punishment will hit those of them who disbelieved. There is no blame on the weak, nor on the sick, nor on those who find nothing to spend, when they are loyal to God and His Messenger. There is no way against the good-doers. God is Forgiving, Merciful. Nor on those who when they came to you that you might mount them, you said: I find nothing to mount you on. They turned away, their eyes overflowing with tears of grief that they found nothing to spend.
The way is only against those who ask your leave while they are rich. They were pleased to be with those who stay behind. God has sealed their hearts, so they do not know.

They will make excuses to you when you return to them. Say: do not make excuse. We will not believe you. God has already told us of your news. God will see your work, and His Messenger, then you will be returned to the Knower of the hidden and the witnessed, and He will tell you what you used to do. They will swear to you by God when you return to them, that you may turn from them. Turn from them. They are filth. Their refuge is Hell, a recompense for what they have been earning. They swear to you that you may be pleased with them. If you are pleased with them, God is not pleased with the wicked people.

The desert-Arabs are stronger in unbelief and hypocrisy, and more apt not to know the limits of what God has sent down on His Messenger. God is Knowing, Wise. Among the desert-Arabs are those who take what they spend as a levy, and wait for turns of fortune against you. Upon them is the turn of evil. God is Hearing, Knowing. Among the desert-Arabs are those who believe in God and the Last Day and take what they spend as offerings near to God and to the Messenger’s prayers. Know: it is an offering for them. God will admit them to His mercy. God is Forgiving, Merciful.

90 excuses from aʿrāb; liars sat. 91–92 no blame: weak, sick, those with nothing to spend if loyal; those who came to be mounted, turned away weeping. 93 way only against the rich who ask leave. 94–96 on return: we will not believe your excuse; God and His Messenger will see your work; they are rijs; if you are pleased God is not. 97 aʿrāb stronger in kufr and nifāq; less knowing of the ḥudūd sent down on the Messenger. 98–99 two kinds of aʿrāb: spend as a fine and wait disasters; spend as offering near to God and the Messenger’s prayers.

Aʿrāb (desert-Arabs / Bedouin) arrive with excuses. Those who lied to God and His Messenger sat. No blame: weak, sick, those who find nothing to spend — if they are loyal (naṣaḥū) to God and His Messenger. No way against the good-doers. Nor those who asked to be mounted and were told there was nothing; they left in tears. The way is only against the rich who ask leave and prefer the sitters. Sealed hearts.

On return they will excuse and swear. Do not believe them. God has told their news. God will see your work, and His Messenger — then return to the Knower of ghayb and shahāda. They are rijs (filth). Hell. They swear that you may be pleased. If you are pleased with them, God is not pleased with the wicked. The Messenger’s being pleased is here not sufficient. God can withhold pleasure the Messenger might grant. That sits on Pole B of the authority frame without cancelling Pole A.

As a class they are stronger in unbelief and hypocrisy and likelier not to know the limits sent down on His Messenger. Then a split: some treat spending as a maghram (levy/fine) and wait the dawāʾir against you; the evil turn is on them. Some believe in God and the Last Day and treat spending as qurubāt with God and with the Messenger’s ṣalawāt (prayers / blessings). That is an offering for them; He will admit them to mercy. The aʿrāb are not one verdict.
al-aʿrāb. muʿadhdhirūn. lā ḥaraja. naṣaḥū. mā aḥmilukum ʿalayhi. dhawū l-ṭawl. rijs. aʿrābu ashaddu kufran wa-nifāqan. ḥudūd. maghram. dawāʾir. qurubāt. ṣalawāt al-rasūl.
SI: bedouins. Haleem: desert Arabs. Pickthall: wandering Arabs. Arberry: Bedouins.
a'rab = desert-Arab / Bedouin collectivity. Not every Arab.
SI: [they are] sincere. Haleem: true to. Pickthall: true to. Arberry: faithful to.
n-s-h: loyal counsel / sincerity toward God and Messenger.
SI: impurity. Haleem: filth. Pickthall: unclean. Arberry: an abomination.
Same root-family as 9:28 najas, not the same word.
SI: even if you are satisfied with them. Haleem: even if you are happy with them. Pickthall: though thou be pleased with them. Arberry: though thou art pleased with them.
SI: the Messenger's prayers. Haleem: the Messenger's prayer. Pickthall: the prayers of the messenger. Arberry: the prayers of the Messenger.
His ṣalawāt as a hoped-for nearness, next to qurubāt with God.
Yusuf Ali 9:99 line only: 'and the prayers of the Messenger.'

Excuse is sorted: weak/sick/penniless loyalists and the weeping unmounted are clear. Rich sitters are not. On return, their oaths are refused in advance. God and His Messenger will see the work — then God tells. If the Messenger were pleased, God still would not be pleased with the wicked. That is Pole B again. Aʿrāb as a class: harsher kufr/nifāq, weaker grasp of ḥudūd sent down on the Messenger. Then two kinds inside the class: spend-as-fine vs spend-as-nearness plus the Messenger’s prayers.
9:28 najas. 9:61–63 please God and Messenger. 9:96 inverts that pair for this class. QB-0272 Messenger-pleasure insufficient vs God’s displeasure. QB-0273 aʿrāb split, not a single verdict.
A'rab excuses; liars sat; no blame on weak/sick/penniless if loyal
Those who asked to be mounted left weeping
Way only against the rich who ask leave
On return: do not believe them; they are rijs; if you are pleased God is not
A'rab stronger in kufr and nifaq; less knowing of hudud sent on the Messenger
Two a'rab: spend as levy vs spend as nearness plus the Messenger's prayers
9:100–110 — first of the emigrants and helpers; mixed deeds; deferred; the mosque built for harm.

packets.title: S009 Al-Tawba CP09 vv100-110
paragraphs: The first ones, the first of the emigrants and the helpers, and those who followed them in good-doing — God is pleased with them and they are pleased with Him. He has prepared for them gardens under which rivers flow, abiding in them forever. That is the great triumph.

Among those around you of the desert-Arabs are hypocrites, and of the people of the City. They persist in hypocrisy. You do not know them. We know them. We will punish them twice, then they will be returned to a great punishment.

Others have confessed their sins. They mixed a righteous deed with another that was bad. God may turn to them. God is Forgiving, Merciful. Take from their wealth a ṣadaqa that you cleanse them and purify them by it, and pray over them. Your prayer is a sakīna for them. God is Hearing, Knowing. Do they not know that God is He who accepts repentance from His servants and takes the ṣadaqāt, and that God is the Relenting, the Merciful.
Say: work. God will see your work, and His Messenger, and the believers. Then you will be returned to the Knower of the hidden and the witnessed, and He will tell you what you used to do.
Others are deferred to God’s command: whether He punishes them or turns to them. God is Knowing, Wise.

Those who took a mosque for harm and unbelief and division among the believers, and as an ambush for whoever warred God and His Messenger before — they will surely swear: we meant only good. God testifies they are liars. Do not stand in it, ever. A mosque founded on godfearing from the first day is worthier that you stand in it. In it are men who love to purify themselves. God loves those who purify themselves. Is one who founded his building on godfearing from God and pleasure better, or one who founded his building on the brink of a crumbling bank that collapsed with him into the fire of Hell? God does not guide the wrongdoing people. The building they built will not cease to be a doubt in their hearts unless their hearts are cut to pieces. God is Knowing, Wise.

100 first emigrants, helpers, and good followers — mutual pleasure with God; gardens. 101 hidden hypocrites among nearby aʿrāb and the City; you do not know them; punished twice. 102–104 confessed mixed deeds; take ṣadaqa; your prayer is sakīna; God takes the ṣadaqāt. 105 work: God, Messenger, believers will see. 106 deferred to God’s command. 107–110 harm-mosque: ḍirār, kufr, tafriq, irṣād for one who warred God and His Messenger before; do not stand in it; taqwā-mosque from the first day; crumbling bank into Hell; the building remains a doubt until hearts are cut.

Al-sābiqūn al-awwalūn of the muhājirīn and the anṣār, and those who followed them in iḥsān. God pleased with them; they with Him. This is the walked charter-verse for the first two communities plus good followers. Later Sunni ʿadālat al-ṣaḥāba arguments lean on it. Level 1 names the first and those who followed in good-doing — not every later claimant.

Hidden hypocrites you do not know; We know; punished twice. Confessors who mixed a good deed and a bad; take ṣadaqa from their wealth to cleanse; pray over them; your ṣalāt is sakīna. God accepts tawba and takes the ṣadaqāt. Work: seen by God, His Messenger, and the believers. Others murjawna li-amri llāh — deferred to His command, punish or turn. The Messenger does not close every file. Some are held for God.

A mosque taken for harm (ḍirār), unbelief, splitting the believers, and as a watch-post for one who warred God and His Messenger before. They swear we meant only good. Do not stand in it, ever. A mosque founded on taqwā from the first day is worthier — men who love to purify. Founding on taqwā and pleasure vs founding on a crumbling bank that dumps into Hell. The building itself remains a doubt in their hearts until hearts are cut. Traditional name: Masjid al-Ḍirār. The verse does not use that title. Standing is barred the way funeral-standing was barred in 9:84.
al-sābiqūn al-awwalūn. al-muhājirūn / al-anṣār. iḥsān. maraḍū ʿalā l-nifāq. khalaṭū ʿamalan ṣāliḥan wa-ākhara sayyiʾan. ṣalli ʿalayhim. murjawna. masjid ḍirāran. tafriq. irṣād. shafā jurufin hār.
SI: the first forerunners. Haleem: the first of those to lead the way. Pickthall: the first to lead the way. Arberry: the first of the first.
First of the first among emigrants and helpers, plus good followers.

SI: pray over them; indeed your prayer is reassurance. Haleem: pray for them; your prayer brings them relief. Pickthall: pray for them; thy prayer is an assuagement. Arberry: pray for them; thy prayers are a comfort.
sakan / sakina-cousin. His prayer here is comfort for the confessors — contrast 9:84.
SI: deferred until the command of Allah. Haleem: waiting for God's decree. Pickthall: wait according to the commandment of Allah. Arberry: deferred to God's commandment.
Files held open. Punish or turn.
SI: a mosque for causing harm. Haleem: a mosque to cause harm. Pickthall: a place of worship out of opposition. Arberry: a mosque in opposition and unbelief.
dirar = harm / opposition. Four purposes named.
SI: Do not stand [in prayer] in it, ever. Haleem: Do not set foot in it. Pickthall: Stand not forth. Arberry: Stand not therein, ever.
Same abadan as 9:84. Haleem's 'set foot' is broader than stand-in-prayer.
Yusuf Ali 9:107 line only: 'a mosque to cause harm and for unbelief...'

First emigrants, helpers, and good followers: mutual pleasure with God. Hidden hypocrites exist even in the City; the Messenger does not know them all (Pole B / 7:188 cousin). Confessors can be cleansed by ṣadaqa and by his prayer. Some files stay open for God. A mosque can be built as harm, split, and ambush; standing in it is barred forever; another mosque founded on taqwā from day one is the place to stand. Architecture does not prove intent.

8:72 hijra-walāya. 9:84 no stand at grave. 9:18 who may maintain mosques. QB-0274 first-emigrants-and-helpers charter. QB-0275 you do not know them — limit on the Messenger’s knowledge of inner files. QB-0276 harm-mosque vs taqwā-mosque.
First emigrants, helpers, good followers: God pleased and they pleased
Hidden hypocrites among nearby a'rab and the City; you do not know them
Confessors mixed good and bad; take sadaqa; your prayer is sakina
Work seen by God, Messenger, believers
Mosque for harm, kufr, split, ambush; do not stand in it ever
Taqwa-mosque from the first day; crumbling bank into Hell
You do not know them — knowledge limit
9:111–129 — God has bought the believers; tawba; do not ask for the associators; close of the surah.

packets.title: S009 Al-Tawba CP10 vv111-129
paragraphs: God has purchased from the believers their persons and their property: they have the Garden. They fight in God’s path: they kill and are killed. A promise binding on Him in the Tawrāt and the Injīl and the Quran. Who is more faithful to his compact than God? Rejoice in the bargain you have made. That is the great triumph.
Those who turn, who worship, who praise, who travel, who bow, who prostrate, who bid the right and forbid the wrong, who keep God’s limits — give good news to the believers.

It is not for the Prophet and those who believed to ask forgiveness for the associators, even if they were near of kin, after it has become clear to them that they are companions of Hell. Abraham’s asking forgiveness for his father was only because of a promise he had promised him. When it became clear to him that he was an enemy of God, he dissociated from him. Abraham was tender-hearted, forbearing. God would not send a people astray after He has guided them until He makes clear to them what they should fear. God is of all things Knowing. God — His is the kingdom of the heavens and the earth. He gives life and causes death. You have besides God no friend and no helper.

God has turned to the Prophet and the emigrants and the helpers who followed him in the hour of difficulty, after the hearts of a party of them had almost swerved. Then He turned to them. He is with them Kind, Merciful. And to the three who were left behind, until the earth was strait for them with all its breadth, and their selves were strait for them, and they thought that there is no refuge from God except to Him. Then He turned to them that they might turn. God is the Relenting, the Merciful.

O you who believe, fear God and be with the truthful. It was not for the people of the City and those around them of the desert-Arabs to stay behind the Messenger of God or to prefer their selves to his self. That is because they are not hit by thirst or fatigue or hunger in God’s path, nor do they tread a step that enrages the unbelievers, nor do they take from an enemy a taking, except that it is written for them as a righteous deed. God does not waste the wage of the good-doers. They do not spend a spend, small or great, nor cross a valley, except it is written for them, that God may recompense them better than what they were doing.

It is not for the believers to go forth all together. Why should not a party from each section of them go forth, that they may become learned in the religion and warn their people when they return to them, that they may beware.

O you who believe, fight those who are near you of the unbelievers, and let them find harshness in you. Know that God is with the God-fearing. When a sūra is sent down, some of them say: which of you has this increased in faith? As for those who believe, it has increased them in faith and they rejoice. As for those in whose hearts is disease, it has increased them in filth upon their filth, and they die while they are unbelievers. Do they not see that they are tried every year once or twice? Then they do not turn and they do not remember. When a sūra is sent down, they look at one another: does anyone see you? Then they turn away. God has turned away their hearts, because they are a people who do not understand.

There has come to you a Messenger from yourselves. Grievous to him is what you suffer. Anxious over you. To the believers kind, merciful. If they turn away, say: God is sufficient for me. There is no god but He. On Him I have relied. He is Lord of the great Throne.

111–112 purchase; fight-kill-killed; promise in Tawrat, Injil, Quran; portrait of the purchased. 113–116 no forgiveness-ask for associators even kin; Abraham and his father; God does not send astray after guidance until He makes clear. 117–118 tawba to Prophet, emigrants, helpers in the hour of difficulty; the three left behind until earth and selves were strait. 119–121 with the truthful; City and nearby aʿrāb not to stay behind the Messenger or prefer themselves to him; every thirst, step, spend written. 122 not all go forth; a party stays to learn the din. 123 fight nearby unbelievers; harshness. 124–127 sūra increases faith or filth; they glance and slip away. 128–129 Messenger from yourselves; if they turn, God is sufficient.
9:111 the purchase and the three books

God bought from the believers their persons and property against the Garden. They fight: kill and are killed. A promise binding on Him in the Tawrāt and the Injīl and the Quran. This is a new 7:157-cluster cousin: the purchase-bargain is said to be written in all three. Same test as 7:157 applies — is that bargain locatable in the books Jews and Christians had. Living snapshot: park a find-test next to Problem_7_157. Do not spend it here.

Not for the Prophet and the believers to ask forgiveness for associators, even kin, after it is clear they are companions of Hell. Abraham’s istighfār for his father was only because of a promise. When it was clear he was God’s enemy, he dissociated (tabarraʾa). Cousin of 9:1 baraʾa and of 9:80 seventy-cap. Kin does not override a clear Fire-verdict.

God turned to the Prophet and the emigrants and helpers who followed him in the hour of difficulty, after a party’s hearts almost swerved. And to the three who were left behind until the earth was strait and their selves were strait and they knew there is no refuge from God except to Him. Then He turned that they might turn. Traditional names (Kaʿb and two) are tafsīr. Level 1: three, left behind, then received.

Not all believers go forth. Why not a party from each section go, that they may understand the religion and warn their people when they return. Mobilization in this surah is not total every time. A learning-remainder is commanded.

A Messenger from yourselves. What you suffer is grievous to him. Anxious over you. Kind, merciful to the believers. If they turn away: God is sufficient for me. No god but He. I rely. Lord of the great Throne. The surah that opened with baraʾa and no basmala closes on sufficiency and the Throne.

ishtarā. yaqtulūna wa-yuqtalūn. waʿdan ʿalayhi ḥaqqan fī l-Tawrāti wa-l-Injīli wa-l-Quran. ḥāfiẓūna li-ḥudūd Allāh. yastaghfirū. tabarraʾa. sāʿat al-ʿusra. al-thalāthatu lladhīna khullifū. nafara. li-yatafaqqahū fī l-dīn. ʿazīzun ʿalayhi mā ʿanittum. ḥarīṣun ʿalaykum. ḥasbiya llāh. al-ʿarsh al-ʿaẓīm.

SI: purchased ... they fight ... they kill and are killed. Haleem: bought ... they fight ... kill and are killed. Pickthall: hath bought ... they fight ... slay and are slain. Arberry: has bought ... they fight ... kill and are killed.
Bargain: selves and property for the Garden. Both directions of killing.
All four name Torah, Gospel, Quran.
Same three-name file as 7:157. Find-test parked.

SI: not for the Prophet and those who believe to ask forgiveness for the polytheists, even if they were relatives. Haleem: ... even relatives. Pickthall: ... even though they be their nearest kin. Arberry: ... though they be near kinsmen.
Kin-limit on istighfar after Fire is clear.
SI: obtain understanding in the religion. Haleem: gain understanding of the religion. Pickthall: become learned in religion. Arberry: become learned in religion.
A remainder stays to learn and warn.
SI: from among yourselves ... concerned over you. Haleem: from among yourselves ... full of concern. Pickthall: of yourselves ... anxious. Arberry: of yourselves ... anxious over you.
Yusuf Ali 9:111 line only: 'The promise of this is to be found in the Torah, the Gospel, and the Quran.'

Selves and property are sold for the Garden; the fight kills both ways; the bargain is said to stand in three books. Istighfār for associators stops when Fire is clear, kin included; Abraham’s father is the worked example. Tawba reaches the Prophet himself, the two first communities in the hard hour, and three who had been left behind. Not everyone marches; some stay to learn. Nearby unbelievers are to find harshness. A sūra splits: faith up, or filth up. The Messenger is from them, burdened by their suffering, then told: if they turn, God is enough.

7:157 written with them. Problem_7_157 file. 9:80 seventy. 6:74 Abraham and Āzar already. 19:41–48 parked. QB-0277 purchase promised in Tawrat/Injil/Quran — find-test PARKED with 7:157. QB-0278 istighfar-bar even for kin. QB-0279 tawba includes the Prophet and three left behind. QB-0280 not-all-go-forth vs 9:38–39 go-forth-or-be-replaced — both walked; situation-sorted, not silent naskh.
God purchased selves and property for the Garden; they kill and are killed
Promise binding in Tawrat, Injil, and Quran
No istighfar for associators even kin once Fire is clear
Abraham's ask for his father was a promise; then he dissociated
Tawba to Prophet, emigrants, helpers in the hard hour; and to the three
City and a'rab not to stay behind the Messenger or prefer themselves
Not all go forth; a party stays to learn the din and warn
Fight nearby unbelievers; let them find harshness
A sura increases faith or filth
A Messenger from yourselves; if they turn, God is sufficient
Tawba includes the Prophet and the three
S009 complete. Opened without basmala, with baraʾa. Closed on ḥasbiya llāh and the Throne. Canonical next: S010 Yūnus 10:1.

pickthall.name: The Meaning of the Glorious Koran

verses.arabic: بَرَآءَةٌۭ مِّنَ ٱللَّهِ وَرَسُولِهِۦٓ إِلَى ٱلَّذِينَ عَٰهَدتُّم مِّنَ ٱلْمُشْرِكِينَ
verses.itani: A declaration of immunity from God and His Messenger to the polytheists with whom you had made a treaty.
verses.pickthall: Freedom from obligation (is proclaimed) from Allah and His messenger toward those of the idolaters with whom ye made a treaty.

verses.arabic: فَسِيحُوا۟ فِى ٱلْأَرْضِ أَرْبَعَةَ أَشْهُرٍۢ وَٱعْلَمُوٓا۟ أَنَّكُمْ غَيْرُ مُعْجِزِى ٱللَّهِ ۙ وَأَنَّ ٱللَّهَ مُخْزِى ٱلْكَٰفِرِينَ
verses.itani: So travel the land for four months, and know that you cannot escape God, and that God will disgrace the disbelievers.
verses.pickthall: Travel freely in the land four months, and know that ye cannot escape Allah and that Allah will confound the disbelievers (in His Guidance).

verses.arabic: وَأَذَٰنٌۭ مِّنَ ٱللَّهِ وَرَسُولِهِۦٓ إِلَى ٱلنَّاسِ يَوْمَ ٱلْحَجِّ ٱلْأَكْبَرِ أَنَّ ٱللَّهَ بَرِىٓءٌۭ مِّنَ ٱلْمُشْرِكِينَ ۙ وَرَسُولُهُۥ ۚ فَإِن تُبْتُمْ فَهُوَ خَيْرٌۭ لَّكُمْ ۖ وَإِن تَوَلَّيْتُمْ فَٱعْلَمُوٓا۟ أَنَّكُمْ غَيْرُ مُعْجِزِى ٱللَّهِ ۗ وَبَشِّرِ ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا۟ بِعَذَابٍ أَلِيمٍ
verses.itani: And a proclamation from God and His Messenger to the people on the day of the Greater Pilgrimage, that God has disowned the polytheists, and so did His Messenger. If you repent, it will be better for you. But if you turn away, know that you cannot escape God. And announce to those who disbelieve a painful punishment.
verses.pickthall: And a proclamation from Allah and His messenger to all men on the day of the Greater Pilgrimage that Allah is free from obligation to the idolaters, and (so is) His messenger. So, if ye repent, it will be better for you; but if ye are averse, then know that ye cannot escape Allah. Give tidings (O Muhammad) of a painful doom to those who disbelieve,

verses.arabic: إِلَّا ٱلَّذِينَ عَٰهَدتُّم مِّنَ ٱلْمُشْرِكِينَ ثُمَّ لَمْ يَنقُصُوكُمْ شَيْـًۭٔا وَلَمْ يُظَٰهِرُوا۟ عَلَيْكُمْ أَحَدًۭا فَأَتِمُّوٓا۟ إِلَيْهِمْ عَهْدَهُمْ إِلَىٰ مُدَّتِهِمْ ۚ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ يُحِبُّ ٱلْمُتَّقِينَ
verses.itani: Except for those among the polytheists with whom you had made a treaty, and did not violate any of its terms, nor aided anyone against you. So fulfill the treaty with them to the end of its term. God loves the righteous.
verses.pickthall: Excepting those of the idolaters with whom ye (Muslims) have a treaty, and who have since abated nothing of your right nor have supported anyone against you. (As for these), fulfil their treaty to them till their term. Lo! Allah loveth those who keep their duty (unto Him).

verses.arabic: فَإِذَا ٱنسَلَخَ ٱلْأَشْهُرُ ٱلْحُرُمُ فَٱقْتُلُوا۟ ٱلْمُشْرِكِينَ حَيْثُ وَجَدتُّمُوهُمْ وَخُذُوهُمْ وَٱحْصُرُوهُمْ وَٱقْعُدُوا۟ لَهُمْ كُلَّ مَرْصَدٍۢ ۚ فَإِن تَابُوا۟ وَأَقَامُوا۟ ٱلصَّلَوٰةَ وَءَاتَوُا۟ ٱلزَّكَوٰةَ فَخَلُّوا۟ سَبِيلَهُمْ ۚ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ غَفُورٌۭ رَّحِيمٌۭ
verses.itani: When the Sacred Months have passed, kill the polytheists wherever you find them. And capture them, and besiege them, and lie in wait for them at every ambush. But if they repent, and perform the prayers, and pay the alms, then let them go their way. God is Most Forgiving, Most Merciful.
verses.pickthall: Then, when the sacred months have passed, slay the idolaters wherever ye find them, and take them (captive), and besiege them, and prepare for them each ambush. But if they repent and establish worship and pay the poor-due, then leave their way free. Lo! Allah is Forgiving, Merciful.

verses.arabic: وَإِنْ أَحَدٌۭ مِّنَ ٱلْمُشْرِكِينَ ٱسْتَجَارَكَ فَأَجِرْهُ حَتَّىٰ يَسْمَعَ كَلَٰمَ ٱللَّهِ ثُمَّ أَبْلِغْهُ مَأْمَنَهُۥ ۚ ذَٰلِكَ بِأَنَّهُمْ قَوْمٌۭ لَّا يَعْلَمُونَ
verses.itani: And if anyone of the polytheists asks you for protection, give him protection so that he may hear the Word of God; then escort him to his place of safety. That is because they are a people who do not know.
verses.pickthall: And if anyone of the idolaters seeketh thy protection (O Muhammad), then protect him so that he may hear the Word of Allah, and afterward convey him to his place of safety. That is because they are a folk who know not.

verses.arabic: كَيْفَ يَكُونُ لِلْمُشْرِكِينَ عَهْدٌ عِندَ ٱللَّهِ وَعِندَ رَسُولِهِۦٓ إِلَّا ٱلَّذِينَ عَٰهَدتُّمْ عِندَ ٱلْمَسْجِدِ ٱلْحَرَامِ ۖ فَمَا ٱسْتَقَٰمُوا۟ لَكُمْ فَٱسْتَقِيمُوا۟ لَهُمْ ۚ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ يُحِبُّ ٱلْمُتَّقِينَ
verses.itani: How can there be a treaty with the polytheists on the part of God and His Messenger, except for those with whom you made a treaty at the Sacred Mosque? As long as they are upright with you, be upright with them. God loves the pious.
verses.pickthall: How can there be a treaty with Allah and with His messenger for the idolaters save those with whom ye made a treaty at the Inviolable Place of Worship? So long as they are true to you, be true to them. Lo! Allah loveth those who keep their duty.

verses.arabic: كَيْفَ وَإِن يَظْهَرُوا۟ عَلَيْكُمْ لَا يَرْقُبُوا۟ فِيكُمْ إِلًّۭا وَلَا ذِمَّةًۭ ۚ يُرْضُونَكُم بِأَفْوَٰهِهِمْ وَتَأْبَىٰ قُلُوبُهُمْ وَأَكْثَرُهُمْ فَٰسِقُونَ
verses.itani: How? Whenever they overcome you, they respect neither kinship nor treaty with you. They satisfy you with lip service, but their hearts refuse, and most of them are immoral.
verses.pickthall: How (can there be any treaty for the others) when, if they have the upper hand of you, they regard not pact nor honour in respect of you? They satisfy you with their mouths the while their hearts refuse. And most of them are wrongdoers.

verses.arabic: ٱشْتَرَوْا۟ بِـَٔايَٰتِ ٱللَّهِ ثَمَنًۭا قَلِيلًۭا فَصَدُّوا۟ عَن سَبِيلِهِۦٓ ۚ إِنَّهُمْ سَآءَ مَا كَانُوا۟ يَعْمَلُونَ
verses.itani: They traded away God's revelations for a cheap price, so they barred others from His path. How evil is what they did.
verses.pickthall: They have purchased with the revelations of Allah a little gain, so they debar (men) from His way. Lo! evil is that which they are wont to do.

verses.arabic: لَا يَرْقُبُونَ فِى مُؤْمِنٍ إِلًّۭا وَلَا ذِمَّةًۭ ۚ وَأُو۟لَٰٓئِكَ هُمُ ٱلْمُعْتَدُونَ
verses.itani: Towards a believer they respect neither kinship nor treaty. These are the transgressors.
verses.pickthall: And they observe toward a believer neither pact nor honour. These are they who are transgressors.

verses.arabic: فَإِن تَابُوا۟ وَأَقَامُوا۟ ٱلصَّلَوٰةَ وَءَاتَوُا۟ ٱلزَّكَوٰةَ فَإِخْوَٰنُكُمْ فِى ٱلدِّينِ ۗ وَنُفَصِّلُ ٱلْءَايَٰتِ لِقَوْمٍۢ يَعْلَمُونَ
verses.itani: But if they repent, and perform the prayers, and give the obligatory charity, then they are your brethren in faith. We detail the revelations for a people who know.
verses.pickthall: But if they repent and establish worship and pay the poor-due, then are they your brethren in religion. We detail Our revelations for a people who have knowledge.

verses.arabic: وَإِن نَّكَثُوٓا۟ أَيْمَٰنَهُم مِّنۢ بَعْدِ عَهْدِهِمْ وَطَعَنُوا۟ فِى دِينِكُمْ فَقَٰتِلُوٓا۟ أَئِمَّةَ ٱلْكُفْرِ ۙ إِنَّهُمْ لَآ أَيْمَٰنَ لَهُمْ لَعَلَّهُمْ يَنتَهُونَ
verses.itani: But if they violate their oaths after their pledge, and attack your religion, then fight the leaders of disbelief—they have no faith—so that they may desist.
verses.pickthall: And if they break their pledges after their treaty (hath been made with you) and assail your religion, then fight the heads of disbelief - Lo! they have no binding oaths - in order that they may desist.

verses.arabic: أَلَا تُقَٰتِلُونَ قَوْمًۭا نَّكَثُوٓا۟ أَيْمَٰنَهُمْ وَهَمُّوا۟ بِإِخْرَاجِ ٱلرَّسُولِ وَهُم بَدَءُوكُمْ أَوَّلَ مَرَّةٍ ۚ أَتَخْشَوْنَهُمْ ۚ فَٱللَّهُ أَحَقُّ أَن تَخْشَوْهُ إِن كُنتُم مُّؤْمِنِينَ
verses.itani: Will you not fight a people who violated their oaths, and planned to exile the Messenger, and initiated hostilities against you? Do you fear them? It is God you should fear, if you are believers.
verses.pickthall: Will ye not fight a folk who broke their solemn pledges, and purposed to drive out the messenger and did attack you first? What! Fear ye them? Now Allah hath more right that ye should fear Him, if ye are believers

verses.arabic: قَٰتِلُوهُمْ يُعَذِّبْهُمُ ٱللَّهُ بِأَيْدِيكُمْ وَيُخْزِهِمْ وَيَنصُرْكُمْ عَلَيْهِمْ وَيَشْفِ صُدُورَ قَوْمٍۢ مُّؤْمِنِينَ
verses.itani: Fight them. God will punish them at your hands, and humiliate them, and help you against them, and heal the hearts of a believing people.
verses.pickthall: Fight them! Allah will chastise them at your hands, and He will lay them low and give you victory over them, and He will heal the breasts of folk who are believers.

verses.arabic: وَيُذْهِبْ غَيْظَ قُلُوبِهِمْ ۗ وَيَتُوبُ ٱللَّهُ عَلَىٰ مَن يَشَآءُ ۗ وَٱللَّهُ عَلِيمٌ حَكِيمٌ
verses.itani: And He will remove the anger of their hearts. God redeems whomever He wills. God is Knowledgeable and Wise.
verses.pickthall: And He will remove the anger of their hearts. Allah relenteth toward whom He will. Allah is Knower, Wise.

verses.arabic: أَمْ حَسِبْتُمْ أَن تُتْرَكُوا۟ وَلَمَّا يَعْلَمِ ٱللَّهُ ٱلَّذِينَ جَٰهَدُوا۟ مِنكُمْ وَلَمْ يَتَّخِذُوا۟ مِن دُونِ ٱللَّهِ وَلَا رَسُولِهِۦ وَلَا ٱلْمُؤْمِنِينَ وَلِيجَةًۭ ۚ وَٱللَّهُ خَبِيرٌۢ بِمَا تَعْمَلُونَ
verses.itani: Or do you think that you will be left alone, without God identifying which of you will strive, and take no supporters apart from God, His Messenger, and the believers? God is well Aware of what you do.
verses.pickthall: Or deemed ye that ye would be left (in peace) when Allah yet knoweth not those of you who strive, choosing for familiar none save Allah and His messenger and the believers? Allah is Informed of what ye do.

verses.arabic: مَا كَانَ لِلْمُشْرِكِينَ أَن يَعْمُرُوا۟ مَسَٰجِدَ ٱللَّهِ شَٰهِدِينَ عَلَىٰٓ أَنفُسِهِم بِٱلْكُفْرِ ۚ أُو۟لَٰٓئِكَ حَبِطَتْ أَعْمَٰلُهُمْ وَفِى ٱلنَّارِ هُمْ خَٰلِدُونَ
verses.itani: It is not for the polytheists to attend God’s places of worship while professing their disbelief. These—their works are in vain, and in the Fire they will abide.
